title: Basic Validations
learning_objectives: Understand different types of data validation in PEGA
Master validation rules and error messaging

introduction.title: Data Validation in PEGA
introduction.text: Data validation ensures that information entered into your PEGA applications is accurate, complete, and follows business rules. This tutorial covers the essential validation techniques that help maintain data quality and provide users with helpful feedback when errors occur.

sections.title: Types of Validation
sections.content: PEGA provides several types of validation to ensure data quality at different levels.

validation_types.description: Ensures that essential fields are not left empty
validation_types.implementation: Set the 'Required' property on field definitions

validation_types.description: Verifies that data follows specific patterns or formats
validation_types.implementation: Use format rules or regular expressions

validation_types.description: Ensures numeric values fall within acceptable ranges
validation_types.implementation: Set minimum and maximum value constraints

validation_types.description: Enforces complex business logic and cross-field dependencies
validation_types.implementation: Create custom validation rules using when conditions

sections.title: Implementing Field Validations
sections.content: Learn how to configure different types of field validations in PEGA.

implementation_steps.description: Configure fields that must be completed
Define format requirements for text fields
actions: Select appropriate field type (Email, Phone, etc.)
Define custom format patterns if needed
Test with valid and invalid inputs
Set inclusive or exclusive range boundaries
Consider edge cases and boundary values

sections.title: Error Messaging Best Practices
sections.content: Effective error messages help users understand and correct validation failures.

messaging_principles.description: Messages should clearly explain what went wrong
messaging_principles.good_example: Email address must include @ symbol and domain (e.g., user@company.com)

messaging_principles.description: Tell users how to fix the problem
messaging_principles.good_example: Password must be at least 8 characters with one number and one special character

messaging_principles.description: Use business terminology, not technical jargon
messaging_principles.good_example: Please enter your phone number with area code

sections.title: Validation Timing
sections.content: Understanding when validations occur helps create better user experiences.

timing_options.description: Validates as users type or leave fields
Validates when users submit the entire form
Validates sections as users complete them

summary.title: Key Takeaways
points: Different validation types serve different data quality needs
Field-level validations should be configured based on data requirements
Error messages should be clear, specific, and actionable
Validation timing affects user experience significantly
Testing validations with various inputs ensures reliability
